identity.meaning: who a person is, or the qualities that make a person or group different from others
identity.example: Moving abroad made her think hard about her identity.

heritage.meaning: the traditions, culture and history that a family or country has had for a long time
heritage.example: He is proud of his Greek heritage.

cultural heritage.meaning: the customs, art and traditions passed down within a particular community or country
cultural heritage.example: The festival celebrates the region's cultural heritage.

influence.meaning: the power to change how someone thinks, behaves or develops; to have such an effect on someone
influence.example: My older brother was a big influence on my choice of career.

personality.meaning: the particular qualities that make someone different from other people
personality.example: She has a warm, friendly personality.

ambitious.meaning: having a strong wish to be successful, powerful or rich
ambitious.example: He's an ambitious young lawyer who wants to become a judge.

ambition.meaning: a strong wish to achieve something, especially success or power
ambition.example: Her ambition is to run her own company.

focused.meaning: giving all your attention and effort to one particular goal or activity
focused.example: She stayed focused on her exams and ignored all distractions.

passport.meaning: an official document that proves your nationality and lets you travel to other countries
passport.example: Don't forget to renew your passport before the trip.

lifestyle.meaning: the way in which a person or group lives, including their habits and activities
lifestyle.example: A healthy lifestyle includes regular exercise and good sleep.

podcast.meaning: a digital audio programme that you can download or stream and listen to online
podcast.example: I listen to a history podcast on my way to work.

individual.meaning: one person, considered separately from the group or society they belong to
individual.example: Every individual has the right to be treated fairly.

belong.meaning: to feel happy and accepted as part of a particular group or place
belong.example: After a few months in the team, I finally felt that I belonged.

persona.meaning: the particular way a person presents themselves to others, which may not show their real character
persona.example: The actor has a calm public persona.

online persona.meaning: the image of yourself that you create and show to other people on the internet
online persona.example: Her online persona is much more confident than she is in real life.

physical appearance.meaning: the way a person's face and body look to other people
physical appearance.example: Employers should not judge people by their physical appearance.

play a part in.meaning: to be one of the things that cause or affect something
play a part in.example: Luck played a part in her success.

pay off.meaning: to bring a good result, especially after a lot of effort or risk
pay off.example: All those evenings of practice finally paid off when she won.

immigrant.meaning: a person who has come to live permanently in a country that is not their own
immigrant.example: His grandparents were immigrants from Poland.

grow up.meaning: to change from a child into an adult, or to spend your childhood in a particular place
grow up.example: She grew up in a small village by the sea.

roots.meaning: the place, culture or family background that a person or their family originally comes from
roots.example: He travelled to Ghana to learn more about his roots.

identify.meaning: to recognise and name someone or something; to feel closely connected to a group or culture (identify with)
identify.example: Many young people identify strongly with their local community.

adventurous.meaning: willing to try new, unusual or exciting things
adventurous.example: We're quite adventurous when we choose where to go on holiday.

stubborn.meaning: determined to do things your own way and refusing to change your mind
stubborn.example: My grandfather is too stubborn to ask for help.

outgoing.meaning: friendly, confident and enjoying meeting and talking to other people
outgoing.example: Her outgoing nature makes her popular in every class.

sociable.meaning: enjoying being with other people and meeting new people
sociable.example: He's very sociable and always organises team dinners.

settle for.meaning: to accept something that is not exactly what you wanted
settle for.example: I won't settle for second best in my career.

co-found.meaning: to start an organisation or business together with one or more other people
co-found.example: She co-founded a charity for young musicians.

award-winning.meaning: having received a prize for being very good
award-winning.example: They run an award-winning restaurant in the city centre.

attitude.meaning: the way you think and feel about something, which affects how you behave
attitude.example: A positive attitude can help you cope with change.

background.meaning: the details of a person's family, education and experience
background.example: People from many different backgrounds work in our team.

get in touch.meaning: to contact someone by phone, email or message
get in touch.example: Please get in touch if you have any questions.

take up.meaning: to start doing a new activity, hobby or job
take up.example: He took up photography after he retired.

get the job done.meaning: to finish a task successfully, even if it is difficult
get the job done.example: We worked through the weekend to get the job done.

get together.meaning: to meet other people in order to spend time together
get together.example: We try to get together every month for dinner.

crazy about.meaning: extremely enthusiastic about someone or something
crazy about.example: My little sister is crazy about horses.

cheerful.meaning: happy and showing it in the way you behave
cheerful.example: The waiter was cheerful even at the end of a long shift.

reliable.meaning: able to be trusted to do what you expect or have promised
reliable.example: She's a reliable colleague who never misses a deadline.

represent.meaning: to speak or act officially for someone, or to show or be a symbol of something
represent.example: The logo represents the company's values.

brand.meaning: a product or company name that is known to the public and sold under its own name
brand.example: They have built a successful fashion brand in only five years.

applicant.meaning: a person who formally asks for something, such as a job or a place on a course
applicant.example: There were over two hundred applicants for the position.

charity.meaning: an organisation that collects money to help people in need
charity.example: She runs a half marathon every year to raise money for charity.

emphasise.meaning: to show that something is especially important or true by giving it special attention
emphasise.example: The report emphasises the need for better training.

duration.meaning: the length of time that something continues
duration.example: Please keep your phone switched off for the duration of the flight.

state verb.meaning: a verb that describes a situation or condition rather than an action, such as know or own
state verb.example: 'Know' is a state verb, so we don't usually say 'I'm knowing'.

suffix.meaning: a group of letters added to the end of a word to make a new word

experienced.meaning: having skill and knowledge because you have done something for a long time
experienced.example: We need an experienced pilot for this route.

relaxed.meaning: calm and not worried or nervous
relaxed.example: He looked relaxed after a week at the beach.

optimistic.meaning: expecting good things to happen in the future
optimistic.example: I'm optimistic that we'll find a solution.

pessimistic.meaning: expecting bad things to happen in the future
pessimistic.example: Don't be so pessimistic; you might pass after all.

realistic.meaning: sensible about what you can achieve and accepting the facts of a situation
realistic.example: It isn't realistic to expect to learn a language in a month.

generous.meaning: willing to give more money, time or help than is usual or expected
generous.example: It was very generous of her to lend us her car.

thoughtful.meaning: showing that you think about and care for other people's feelings and needs
thoughtful.example: What a thoughtful gift; she remembered I love lavender.

practical.meaning: good at dealing with real situations and at doing useful things
practical.example: She's very practical and can fix almost anything at home.

musical.meaning: having a natural ability or interest in music
musical.example: Both of their children are very musical.

talent.meaning: a natural ability to do something well
talent.example: He has a real talent for languages.

talented.meaning: having a natural ability to do something well
talented.example: She is a talented young violinist.

artistic.meaning: good at creating things such as paintings, or showing skill in art
artistic.example: He's very artistic and designs all our posters.

likeable.example: The main character is a likeable rogue.

helpful.example: The staff at the hotel were extremely helpful.

hopeful.meaning: feeling that something good will happen
hopeful.example: We're hopeful that the results will arrive this week.

emotion.meaning: a strong feeling such as love, anger or fear
emotion.example: He found it hard to hide his emotions.

emotional.example: The farewell party was an emotional evening for everyone.

paragliding.meaning: a sport in which you jump from a high place wearing a large parachute-like wing and glide down
paragliding.example: Paragliding over the Alps was the highlight of the trip.

cheer up.meaning: to make someone feel happier, or to become happier
cheer up.example: A phone call from my friend really cheered me up.

set up.meaning: to arrange or prepare equipment, a system or an organisation so that it is ready to use
set up.example: It took an hour to set up the new router.

depend on.meaning: to trust someone to do something for you, or to be decided by something
depend on.example: You can depend on her to keep a secret.

cards.subheading: Who am I? – Family and identity
cards.text: My name is Sydney and I was born in Sacramento, in the USA. My parents are immigrants from China, so I've grown up speaking Mandarin at home but English at school and with my friends. We have family in China so we have always visited regularly. As well as my U.S. identity, I would say that I identify quite strongly with my Asian roots. (1) ______

In my personal life, I would like to think that I'm quite adventurous. I love trying out new experiences. (2) ______ I'm not particularly good at either, but I'm quite stubborn, so I plan to keep going. I'm also outgoing and sociable. (3) ______

In my work, I'm very ambitious. I never settle for anything but the best and always work hard. (4) ______ In terms of my experience, I've been designing websites for over seven years. I co-founded WebDesignSY, an award-winning creative studio. I've designed websites for businesses, charities and individuals. I've also taught several courses in design at the California Institute of Arts and Technology. I love nothing more than thinking of interesting ways to represent you and your brand, so please get in touch.

sections.title: Grammar Bank – present perfect simple and continuous

rules.label: Same time frame
rules.rule: We use both the present perfect simple and the present perfect continuous to talk about situations or actions which started in the past and continue into the present. Sometimes there is no important difference between the two tenses, particularly with verbs such as work, live and study. However, there are also some important differences between the two.
rules.example: Mauro has lived/has been living in Bologna since 2010.

blocks.title: Focusing on the result of the activity

rules.label: Result
rules.rule: We use the present perfect simple to focus on the result of a completed activity.
rules.example: He's passed all of his exams. (Focuses on the result – passing the exams)

rules.label: Activity
rules.rule: We use the present perfect continuous to focus on the activity itself.
rules.example: He's been studying for his exams. (Focuses on the activity of studying)

rules.label: How many? / How much? / How far?
rules.rule: We use the present perfect simple to answer the questions: 'How many?', 'How much?' or 'How far?'
rules.example:
We've interviewed more than 100 applicants. (How many?)
He's raised €1,000 for charity. (How much?)
They've driven over 3,000 kilometres. (How far?)

rules.label: How long?
rules.rule: We use the present perfect continuous to answer the question: 'How long?' and to emphasise that an action has continued for a long time (using for and since to describe the duration), or is repeated. We often use the present perfect continuous with verbs that describe long actions, such as wait, stay, play, sit, stand, write, etc.
rules.example:
We've been waiting for over forty minutes now!
He's been sitting on that bench since this morning.

rules.label: Completed actions
rules.rule: We use the present perfect simple to describe completed actions.
rules.example:
Oh no, I've missed the bus! (The bus has gone, so the action is completed.)
I'm afraid she's left the office. (She isn't here now, so the action is completed.)

rules.label: Unfinished actions
rules.rule: We use the present perfect continuous to describe actions that are unfinished or in progress.
rules.example:
I've been learning Mandarin. (I'm still learning, so the action is not completed.)
She's been trying to speak to you. (She still hasn't spoken to you, so she's still trying.)

rules.label: State verbs
rules.rule: We use the present perfect simple, NOT the present perfect continuous, with state verbs, to talk about states or situations that started in the past and are in progress.
rules.example:
How long have you known Jessica?
I've owned this car since 2009.

rules.label: Experiences and habits
rules.rule: We also use the present perfect simple with the words always, ever and never to talk about experiences and habits.
rules.example:
He's never driven to work, he always goes by bike.
I've always baked my own bread.

blocks.instruction: Choose the correct word(s) to complete the sentences.

items.q: I've ___ this amazing series recently.
items.explanation: A completed activity with a recent result takes the present perfect simple.

items.q: I've ___ to the gym twice already this week!
items.explanation: We count completed occasions with the present perfect simple.

items.q: We've ___ them for about ten years.
items.explanation: State verbs are not used in the continuous form.

items.q: You've ___ on that report all morning!
items.hint: The emphasis is on the long activity.
items.explanation: 'All morning' emphasises the duration of the activity.

items.q: He's ___ with me whilst they finish repainting his flat.
items.hint: The situation is temporary and in progress.
items.explanation: Stay with a temporary, unfinished situation suggests the continuous.

items.q: I've probably ___ that film about twenty-five times!
items.explanation: We use the present perfect simple to say how many times.

blocks.instruction: Complete the sentences with the correct present perfect simple or continuous form of the verb in brackets.

items.q: Oh, no! I think he ___ (break) his foot.
items.explanation: The result matters (the broken foot), so we use the present perfect simple.

items.q: I ___ (cook) all morning, but I've still got a lot to do!
items.explanation: The activity is continuing and unfinished, so we use the present perfect continuous.

items.q: I ___ never ___ (try) skiing.
items.explanation: We use the present perfect simple with never to talk about experiences.

items.q: How many invitations ___ you ___ (send) so far?
items.explanation: How many asks for a number, so we use the present perfect simple.

items.q: ___ all the guests ___ (arrive) yet?
items.explanation: We use the present perfect simple with yet for completed actions.

items.q: I'm worried about Piotr. He ___ (work) so hard recently.
items.hint: The activity is repeated over a period of time.
items.explanation: The emphasis is on the repeated activity, so we use the present perfect continuous.

items.q: How long ___ you ___ (know) Natasha?
items.explanation: Know is a state verb, so we use the present perfect simple.

items.q: She ___ (study) for her exams for weeks.
items.explanation: 'For weeks' emphasises the duration, so we use the present perfect continuous.

blocks.instruction: Use the answers and the verbs in bold to write questions in the present perfect simple or continuous. If both forms are possible, use the continuous form.

items.q: I teach at the university. How long ___ there?
items.hint: Both forms are possible: use the continuous.
items.explanation: Use the present perfect continuous for How long? with an action verb.

items.q: I know Johanna really well. How long ___ her?
items.explanation: Know is a state verb, so we use the present perfect simple.

items.q: I'm developing a new website. How long ___ it?
items.hint: The action is still in progress.
items.explanation: Use the present perfect continuous for How long? with an unfinished action.

items.q: I play golf on Saturdays. How long ___ ?
items.hint: Both forms are possible: use the continuous.
items.explanation: Use the present perfect continuous for a repeated activity with How long?

items.q: I live in Krakow. How long ___ there?
items.hint: Both forms are possible: use the continuous.
items.explanation: With live, both forms are possible, so we use the continuous.

items.q: He wins a lot of awards. How many ___ ?
items.explanation: How many asks for a number, so we use the present perfect simple.

blocks.instruction: Look at how we can form adjectives from verbs and nouns by using different suffixes, e.g. -ed, -ous, -ful.

blocks.prompt: Look at the table. Discuss the questions.
questions: What is the root word for each of the adjectives in the table?

blocks.instruction: Complete the table in Ex 1A with adjectives formed from the verbs and nouns in the box.

items.q: (1) -ed: experienced, relaxed, ___
items.hint: Add -ed to a noun from the box.
items.explanation: talent + -ed = talented.

items.q: (2) -ic: optimistic/pessimistic, realistic, ___
items.explanation: artist + -ic = artistic.

items.q: (3) -ous: generous, ___
items.explanation: adventure + -ous = adventurous (the final e is dropped).

items.q: (4) -ous: generous, ___
items.explanation: ambition + -ous = ambitious.

items.q: (5) -able: reliable, ___
items.hint: You can keep or drop the final -e.
items.explanation: like + -able = likeable or likable.

items.q: (6) -ful: thoughtful, cheerful, ___
items.hint: Add -ful to a verb or noun from the box.
items.explanation: help + -ful = helpful.

items.q: (7) -ful: thoughtful, cheerful, ___
items.hint: Drop the final -e? No: keep the root and add -ful.
items.explanation: hope + -ful = hopeful.

items.q: (8) -al: practical, musical, ___
items.hint: Add -al to a noun from the box.
items.explanation: emotion + -al = emotional.

blocks.instruction: Complete the sentences with the correct adjective form of the words in brackets.

items.q: We can depend on Sam to be here on time. He's very ___ (rely).
items.explanation: rely + -able = reliable (y changes).

items.q: Melissa became quite ___ as she was watching the film. (emotion)
items.explanation: emotion + -al = emotional.

items.q: Al will need some help setting up the new printer. He's not very ___ (practice).
items.explanation: practice becomes practical.

items.q: I love the fact that Leo is always so ___ about life! (optimist)
items.explanation: optimist + -ic = optimistic.

items.q: Sasha is a really ___ musician. (talent)
items.explanation: talent + -ed = talented.

items.q: Thanks for moving those boxes – it was really ___ (help).
items.explanation: help + -ful = helpful.

items.q: It was very ___ of you to send those flowers to cheer me up! (thought)
items.explanation: thought + -ful = thoughtful.

items.q: I don't think I'll go to the party – I'm not feeling very ___ today. (social)
items.explanation: social becomes sociable.

items.q: I'm not ___ enough to go paragliding! (adventure)
items.explanation: adventure becomes adventurous.

items.q: I'm sure she'll be prime minister one day. She's incredibly ___ (ambition).
items.explanation: ambition becomes ambitious.

blocks.instruction: Listen and check your answers.

blocks.prompt: Work in pairs. Take turns describing adjectives for your partner to guess. Student A: This describes someone who plays the guitar and sings, and loves going to watch bands. Student B: Musical? Student A: That's right.
